html:
In the 14th century, by Brunei tradition in the 1360s, the ruler Awang Alak Betatar took up Islam and the name Muhammad Shah. He is counted as the first sultan of Brunei.

Brunei was already a trading port on the northwest coast of Borneo, sending envoys to China. Its conversion came as Muslim traders spread through the islands, at about the time of the rise of Malacca.

Every sultan since claims descent from him, down to Hassanal Bolkiah today. Islam became the core of the Brunei state, later written into its national idea of a Malay Islamic Monarchy. See also Brunei.
